## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sīlavahatthijātaka* (Ja 72), also referred to as the *Sīlavanāgarājajātaka* or *Sīlavanāga*, is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection located at PTS Jātaka i. 319–322 [SuttaCentral; Anandajoti 2010; Trung Huynh 2016; Baba 2012]. According to its opening frame story, the Buddha recounted the tale while residing at the Bamboo-grove in response to the monks discussing Devadatta's ingratitude and failure to recognize the virtues of the Blessed One; the Buddha observed that this was not the first time Devadatta had acted ungratefully toward him [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as a king of elephants who rescues a forester lost in the wilderness; driven by insatiable greed, the forester later returns and repeatedly demands the elephant's tusks, which the Bodhisatta readily surrenders, exemplifying human ingratitude contrasted with the noble character of animals [Anandajoti 2010; Baba 2012].
